subject: general
question: The ______ Five-Year Plan of India completed its term in March 2017.
solution:
The correct answer is __**12th**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **12th Five-Year Plan** of India completed its term in March 2017.
 
• The Five-Year Plans are centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The 12th Five-Year Plan was the last plan, as the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
• The 12th Plan aimed at achieving a growth rate of 8% but only managed to achieve around 7% due to various economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Five-Year Plans were inspired by the Soviet model and were launched by India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on the agricultural sector.
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• With the dissolution of the Planning Commission, the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established to serve as the policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• NITI Aayog aims to foster involvement and participation in the economic policy-making process by the State Governments of India.
